method: Instrument only packed dictionary TextDecoder calls during current owned top-k. Restore the decoder before output materialization. Independently verify selected stable-sort results and final zero admission. Simulate bounded LRU and modulo/mixed direct-mapped directories at capacities 1, 8, 64, 256.
findings: Mostly unique input dictionaries still reuse heap candidates: eight-entry LRU predicts about 51–52% hits for dense cardinality-8192 cases. Cardinality/selected-count heuristics alone miss this reuse.
Modulo direct mapping suffers severe strided-selection collisions, down to approximately 0.5% hits for eight slots.
Multiplicative high-bit mixing avoids that particular collapse, with eight-slot predictions around 43–82% on the larger-dictionary sparse cases; LRU generally retains more hits.
Small repeated dictionaries can approach full hit coverage once directory capacity covers their reachable entries.
scope: Predicted decode avoidance is not speed, retained-memory admission, live heap, or concurrent cloud evidence. Diagnostic simulation bookkeeping is outside the engine allocation pool.
